items.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas
items.abstract: Finding a paper from an informal research idea requires more than matching topic words: relevant work may use different terminology, and its distinguishing mechanism may be absent from the abstract. We present \system{}, an auditable literature-search system built on PaperArena. It combines multi-source discovery, identity verification, facet-based abstract assessment, semantic citation expansion, and joint Expert ranking. A retrieval-only mode ranks up to five papers from a shortlist of at most 60, using complete available abstracts and locally selected PDF evidence from five fixed acquisition attempts, without generating a long-form report. In a historical comparison covering ten queries from each of EASY, MEDIUM, and HARD, aggregate reported Hit@5 is 53.3\% for \system{}, 43.3\% for ChatGPT web Deep Research, and 36.7\% for Gemini web Deep Research under the documented accounting convention. The advantage is concentrated in EASY and MEDIUM; ChatGPT leads on HARD. Selected \system{} runs average 8 minutes 53 seconds, compared with user-reported web averages of 5.2 and 4.7 minutes. A separate nine-query API sample averages \$0.0945 per task; this is a historical cost observation, not a matched comparison with web subscription costs. Pairwise Top 5 coverage ranges from 6\% to 34\%, showing differing returned evidence sets. The system also exposes optional implementation analysis and citation-evolution tools. These results support targeted idea-to-paper retrieval while leaving general web research, forum search, and broader relevance evaluation open. https://github.com/ystok66/IDEA2PRIOR

items.title: IDENTIFIKASI BAHAYA DAN PENILAIAN RISIKO PADA AKTIVITAS LOADING OVERBURDEN MENGGUNAKAN METODE IBPR DI PIT E BANKO TENGAH PT SATRIA BAHANA SARANA TANJUNG ENIM
items.abstract: Abstract: Loading overburden activities at Front Selingsing Pit E Banko Tengah, PT Satria Bahana Sarana, involve heavy equipment, dynamic working conditions, and interactions between excavators and dump trucks that may create occupational hazards. This study aimed to identify hazards, assess risk levels, and determine risk controls using Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA/IBPR). Data were collected through field observation, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires involving 25 respondents. Risk was assessed by multiplying probability and severity based on the company's risk matrix. The findings showed hazards related to working conditions, heavy-equipment movement, and human factors. High-risk conditions included non-standard excavator bench geometry, high-intensity dust exposure, blind spots, and unstable working floors. Risk controls included bench geometry improvement, work-area arrangement, safety signs, equipment-route management, supervision, safety talks, and personal protective equipment. Additional controls reduced residual risk and improved the overall control of loading overburden hazards. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi potensi bahaya, menilai tingkat risiko, dan menentukan upaya pengendalian pada aktivitas loading overburden menggunakan metode Identifikasi Bahaya dan Penilaian Risiko (IBPR). items.title: Identifying Barriers to Using Generative AI in Education Through AI-Assisted Literature Mining of arXiv Articles
items.abstract: This study presents an exploratory, generative AI (GenAI)-assisted full-text analysis of barriers to using GenAI in education within an arXiv corpus. A total of 19,756 records were retrieved using a keyword search and then screened for relevance using three large language models (LLMs), GPT-4o mini, Gemini 2.0 flash-lite, and Llama3-70B (Groq), through a voting mechanism. This yielded a corpus of 1998 education-relevant full-text articles. Using GPT-4o, learning and teaching scenarios (LTSs) were extracted using a structured 6As framework (Actor, Activity, AI Role, AI Interface, Assessment, Achievement) developed for this study. Barrier themes were derived separately by clustering a total of 4729 barrier descriptions, embedded using OpenAI’s embedding model. The descriptive results indicate: (i) STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) vs. non-STEM distributions of GenAI use cases are broadly comparable; (ii) approximately 75% of reported GenAI intervention outcomes were classified as non-negative across the different disciplines; and (iii) reported barriers show different descriptive patterns between STEM and non-STEM disciplines. STEM use cases more frequently report performance constraints, while non-STEM ones more frequently report privacy and workflow integration concerns. The observed disciplinary differences in extracted barriers suggest that approaches to supporting GenAI use may need to vary by disciplinary context. However, the findings are limited by arXiv coverage and limited human validation; future research should broaden source coverage and strengthen robust validation.

items.title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
items.abstract: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. Keywords Artificial intelligence, project planning, project scheduling, project control, construction management, digital transformation

items.title: Impact of Er,Cr:YSGG laser and bonding protocols on enamel surface integrity and bracket bonding strength: an in vitro study
items.abstract: Adequate enamel conditioning is vital for reliable bracket bonding. Laser-assisted alternatives to conventional acid etching exist, but their impact on shear bond strength (SBS) remains highly controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Er,Cr:YSGG laser enamel conditioning on the SBS of orthodontic brackets bonded using different composite materials in the presence or absence of a bonding agent. Thirty-six extracted human premolars and molars were randomly allocated into four groups (n=9). Group A received Er,Cr:YSGG laser conditioning followed by bonding with 3M Universal Bonding Agent (3M ESPE, St. Paul, MN, USA) and 3M composite (3M ESPE, St. Paul, MN, USA). Group B (control) received conventional phosphoric acid etching followed by bonding with 3M Universal Bonding Agent and 3M composite. Group C received Er,Cr:YSGG laser conditioning followed by bonding with Nova composite (Imicryl, Konya, Turkey) without a bonding agent, while Group D received conventional phosphoric acid etching followed by bonding with Nova composite without a bonding agent. SBS testing was performed using a universal testing machine, and failure patterns were qualitatively assessed using the Adhesive Remnant Index (ARI). Artificial intelligence technology of IBM SPSS Statistics software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA) was used for the statistical analysis. The mean SBS values were 13.06±4.20 MPa, 15.29±9.52 MPa, 13.20±8.04 MPa, and 11.41±6.22 MPa for Groups A, B, C, and D, respectively. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed no statistically significant difference among the four groups (F(3,32)=0.428, p=0.734). Although Group B demonstrated the highest mean SBS and Group D the lowest, substantial overlap in standard deviation (SD) values was observed among all groups. The qualitative ARI assessment indicated that the predominant failure mode corresponded to score 2. No significant difference in orthodontic bracket SBS was observed between Er,Cr:YSGG laser conditioning and conventional phosphoric acid etching.

items.title: Impact of hospital design on the perceived well-being of healthcare workers: a scoping review
items.abstract: This scoping review maps the available evidence on how the design of hospital spaces influences the perceived well-being of healthcare workers. Following the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guideline, it addresses the question: "Which aspects of hospital space design influence the perceived well-being of healthcare workers, and in what ways?" Eligible sources are primary studies and literature reviews conducted in hospital settings that relate features of the physical environment (layout, lighting, noise and acoustics, break and recovery spaces, nature and views, ergonomics and furniture, aesthetics) to staff well-being outcomes (stress, burnout, fatigue, job and environmental satisfaction, recovery, comfort, professional relationships and perceived safety). The review is being carried out as a bachelor's thesis in Nursing at the University of Milan. This registration is retrospective: database searches (June 2026), screening and data extraction had already been completed at the time of registration.

items.title: Impact of the Digitalization of Training Processes in the Military Field
items.abstract: This chapter examines how the digitalization of military training affects training costs, maintenance, repairs, and victim compensation in Latin American Armed Forces. Using a qualitative-documentary methodology with analytical and comparative scope, the study reviews scientific literature, institutional reports, multilateral organization documents, and research on military simulation, virtual and augmented reality, cybersecurity, digital government, military spending, and victim reparation. Findings indicate that digital training technologies—such as simulators, virtual platforms, extended reality, artificial intelligence, data analytics, and digital twins—can reduce reliance on real equipment, lower ammunition and fuel consumption, improve maintenance management, enhance learning assessment and traceability, and decrease operational risks. The chapter concludes that digitalization should not replace live training but complement it through a hybrid, progressive, and measurable model that supports defense objectives, cybersecurity, legal compliance, and efficient public spending.

items.title: In-Parameter Learning: Why Lifelong AI Systems Need More Than Longer Context
items.abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to interact with changing users, tools, and environments over extended periods of time. However, current systems remain largely static: their parameters are fixed during deployment, while new experiences, domain knowledge, corrections, and behavioral adaptations are handled primarily through external memory management and in-context learning. In this position paper, we focus on lifelong AI: AI systems that can continually learn from their long-term experience throughout an extended deployment lifetime. This position paper argues that existing in-context mechanisms are insufficient for lifelong AI, and advocate In-Parameter Learning (IPL) as a necessary complement to In-Context Learning (ICL), referring to mechanisms that allow a deployed model to continually and safely update its parameters during use. More broadly, we aim to renew the community’s attention to in-parameter learning and to recalibrate the overly optimistic expectations placed on in-context learning alone. Our central claim is that future lifelong AI systems should be built around a hybrid paradigm: in-context learning for immediate, provisional, and reversible information, and in-parameter learning for durable, cumulative, and generalizable growth.

items.title: Innovación en Inteligencia Artificial y Nuevas Tecnologías en la Medicina del Deporte y el Fútbol
items.abstract: Background: Innovation in artificial intelligence (AI) in sports medicine integrates algorithms, sensors, computer vision, predictive analytics and decision-support systems to improve athlete health, performance, safety and competitive fairness. Objective: To reconstruct the historical development of AI and emerging technologies in sport, assess applications, accuracy, benefits, limitations, ethical dilemmas and rule-related impact, with a focus on association football and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Methods: A rapid historical systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, IEEE Xplore and official FIFA, IFAB, UEFA, IOC and FIMS sources were searched from 1950 to July 2026. Results: Eighty-two sources were synthesized; 47 provided quantitative information. Mature applications included player tracking, video analysis, workload monitoring and officiating support. Injury prediction remained promising but vulnerable to overfitting, poor external validation and dataset shift. Conclusions: AI is most useful as an augmented-intelligence layer supporting clinical, coaching and refereeing expertise. Responsible adoption requires prospective validation, explainability, cybersecurity, athlete consent and clear accountability.

items.title: Innovations, Interdisciplinary Challenges and Future Directions in Harnessing AI for Criminal Justice System
items.abstract: The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming established practices in almost every segment of criminal justice system. Criminal justice system is benefitted in terms of efficiency, allocation of resources and consistency by integration of AI. But the integration of AI elevates significant apprehension of algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability and civil liberties in criminal justice system. The paper aims to critically show the dual nature of AI across criminal justice system. In this work, we have reviewed and given a precise taxonomy covering uses of AI across criminal justice system. Benefits and challenges of AI across the criminal justice system along with AI technologies used in law have also been reviewed and mentioned. Some recommendations for future uses of AI across criminal justice system have been given. We recommend effective governance, stakeholder collaboration, and the creation of transparent, explainable AI models in order to ensure that AI systems fulfill the principles of fairness, due process, and human rights in criminal justice.

items.title: Instances of the Rhetorical Inimitability of the Noble Qurʾan
items.abstract: This article analyses, from the point of view of the science of Qurʾanic studies, the inimitability of the eloquence and the rhetoric of the Noble Qurʾan, the miraculous force of the effect of each of its words and sentences, and the incapacity of humankind before this speech in respect of style. The study discloses, through precise examples of verses and their exegetical and rhetorical commentaries, the impossibility of replacing the Qurʾanic wordings, the phenomenon of their immediate effect upon the heart as the spirit acts upon the body, and the fact that each word has been chosen as lighter in pronunciation and more beautiful in its phonetic quality than its alternatives. The research possesses an important theoretical and methodological significance within the directions of the sciences of the Qurʾan known as the inimitability of the Qurʾan and rhetorical exegesis. It enriches the classical traditions of exegesis and the rules of rhetoric with contemporary methods of textual analysis and forestalls the danger of a superficial and incorrect interpretation of the original meaning of the verses. Furthermore, in a contemporary age in which the generation of text by artificial intelligence and digital communication have developed, the investigation of the mastery of Qurʾanic word-usage establishes upon a scholarly foundation the absolute superiority of the divine speech over any algorithmic or human text. Ten verses of the Noble Qurʾan are analysed in respect of their rhetorical inimitability.

items.title: Institutional and academic determinants of ChatGPT adoption in higher education: evidence from a resource-constrained university context
items.abstract: This study examines the determinants of students’ use of ChatGPT as a learning support tool at a public local university located in a resource-constrained, mountainous region of northern Vietnam, characterised by socioeconomic disadvantage and limited access to educational resources. Drawing on survey data from 906 undergraduate students, the study investigates how individual digital readiness, academic context, institutional support, and economic constraints jointly shape students’ engagement with ChatGPT. The findings indicate that students’ use of ChatGPT is influenced more strongly by academic and institutional conditions than by individual digital competence alone, while economic barriers remain a significant constraint on sustained use. By situating generative AI adoption within a structurally disadvantaged higher education context, this study extends technology acceptance research and underscores the importance of context-sensitive, institution-led strategies to ensure equitable and responsible integration of generative AI in public universities.

items.title: Integrating Heuristic Evaluation and UTAUT2: Uncovering Usability Friction and Behavioral Intention in Public EV Charging Infrastructure
items.abstract: Indonesia’s electric mobility transition relies heavily on Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure (EVCI) and complementary applications such as PLN Mobile. This study evaluates the usability of soft infrastructure interfaces and usage intention across both soft (companion app) and hard (physical charging stations) infrastructure, using an Exploratory Sequential Mixed-Methods design that combines qualitative Heuristic Evaluation (HE) and a quantitative UTAUT2-based PLS-SEM (n = 100). HE identified 21 usability flaws based on Nielsen’s principles, revealing severe raw error messages and ambiguous terminology. Structural model results indicated that adoption drivers—Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Facilitating Conditions, and Hedonic Motivation—had no significant effect on Behavioral Intention. Instead, adoption was influenced by Price Value, Social Influence, and Habit. The findings highlight an adoption pattern shaped by economic value and routine use rather than intrinsic satisfaction, in which severe usability flaws serve as friction points that counterbalance functional drivers. Finally, targeted multi-stakeholder recommendations are outlined for developers, charging operators, hardware designers, and policymakers.

items.title: Integrating Technology, Humanities, and Indian Knowledge Systems for Viksit Bharat’s Higher Education
items.abstract: The vision of a Viksit Bharat sets its higher education system a threefold task: to absorb advancing technology, to sustain the humanising work of the humanities, and to recover the depth of India’s own knowledge traditions. These are often pursued separately, and sometimes as rivals. This paper argues that they are strongest when integrated, and that Indian Knowledge Systems supply the principle by which technology and the humanities may be reconciled. The occasion for the argument is the arrival of generative artificial intelligence in the university, which now performs on demand a large part of what higher education has traditionally taught and assessed summarising, analysing, comparing, and composing often faster than the student examined on these operations. The development forces a question at once practical and philosophical: what does higher education accomplish that a machine cannot, and where should the machine be placed? The answer proposed here returns to a distinction already present in Indian epistemology, the Upaniṣadic difference between aparā vidyā, the lower knowledge of information and the disciplines, and parā vidyā, the higher knowledge that issues in realisation and self-understanding (Radhakrishnan, 1953). Artificial intelligence, it contends, is a powerful instrument of aparā vidyā that cannot enter the domain of parā vidyā, which the university exists to serve. Drawing on the doctoral research from which it arises, the paper synthesises classical Indian aesthetics (Rasa, Dhvani, Vakrokti, and the ideal of the sahr̥daya) and the Vedāntic learning sequence of Śravaṇa–Manana–Nididhyāsana into an integrated framework for higher education, within which technology is assigned a real but bounded role. Its principal field of application is English literary studies, where a brief textual illustration shows how Indian aesthetic categories and a contemplative classroom rhythm may reshape the reading and teaching of literature in an age of intelligent machines. Related throughout to the National Education Policy 2020, the paper concludes that such an integration offers Viksit Bharat a higher education in which the most advanced tools serve, rather than supplant, the oldest ends of learning.

items.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Digital Animation
items.abstract: This article explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in contemporary animation workflows through the analysis of two applied case studies, both directed by the author within the Chilean creative studio Poston Digital Arts. The first case examines the production of an animated title sequence for the science fiction film Affinity, while the second analyzes the development of a commercial spot for the Mortal Kombat x Saucony product collaboration. Both projects involve hybrid production pipelines that combine AI-based tools, such as generative image models, AI-driven motion capture, and AI-assisted storyboarding, with traditional animation techniques. Through comparative analysis, this article identifies advantages in production efficiency, creative iteration, and visual output quality while also recognizing limitations and risks associated with the use of AI. Key findings include the shifting roles within animation teams, the emergence of new professional profiles (such as AI operators and prompt engineers), and the continued importance of human artistic direction. The discussion concludes that AI, when properly integrated, serves as a powerful creative accelerator without replacing the essential role of human oversight, and its use requires conscious management to avoid risks, such as aesthetic homogenization and the erosion of foundational artistic skills.

items.title: Inteligencia artificial autónoma y derecho tributario en Ecuador: diseño de un modelo de gobernanza algorítmica para la determinación fiscal, explicabilidad y protección de los derechos del contribuyente
items.abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) with increasing degrees of autonomy changes how tax administrations detect risk, cross-check information and prepare decisions with individual legal effects. This study designs an algorithmic governance model for tax assessment in Ecuador that combines technological efficiency, explainability and protection of taxpayers’ rights. A qualitative, documentary and comparative legal approach was applied through normative, doctrinal and institutional review of sources published mainly between 2021 and 2026, supplemented by a risk matrix and a layered control design. The findings show that Ecuador has constitutional, tax and data-protection safeguards and, since 2026, general rules applicable to AI systems that process personal data; however, no tax-sector regulation was identified that specifically governs decision-making autonomy, attribution of responsibility and review of high-impact tax actions. The proposed model classifies AI uses by autonomy and risk and requires impact assessment, traceability, individual explainability, verifiable human oversight, auditability and effective remedies. The study concludes that an AI-supported tax decision is legally acceptable only when the administration retains competence and responsibility, can reconstruct the relevant reasoning and provides the taxpayer with a real avenue to understand, contest and obtain review of the decision.

items.title: Intelligent Inverse Design of Meta‐Absorbers Based on Reversible Deep Learning
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Optical meta‐absorbers are artificially engineered materials capable of trapping light in a highly controllable manner, rendering them attractive for a wide range of applications. Artificial intelligence provides powerful tools for the efficient design of such complex structures. Among current methods, tandem neural networks (TNNs) have emerged as a mainstream solution for forward‐inverse modeling. However, TNNs require two separate networks, leading to high computational costs and limited accuracy—particularly in inverse design. In this work, we propose a novel and highly precise design paradigm based on reversible deep learning (RDL), which employs a single, bidirectionally trainable neural network. The RDL framework performs simultaneous training of the inverse and forward models within a unified architecture—addressing structural generation and spectral prediction, and significantly reducing computational costs. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the design of near‐infrared meta‐absorbers using RDL, achieving an order‐of‐magnitude improvement in inverse prediction accuracy compared to TNNs, while using only 66.35% of the training parameters and requiring minimal memory and storage. This study introduces a flexible and efficient platform for the rapid and accurate design of meta‐absorbers tailored to specific absorption spectra, facilitating the intelligent development of advanced optical metamaterials and metadevices.

items.title: International Students’ Agency in Their Use of AI Tools for University Studies: A Qualitative Enquiry
items.abstract: Abstract Recent decades have witnessed the increasing global mobility of higher education students, many of whom seek to advance their careers in their host countries upon graduation. As educational institutions and workplaces integrate generative artificial intelligence (AI) into their systems, it is critical for students to develop AI literacy not only to succeed in their academic studies but also to prepare for AI-driven work environments. However, little is known about how international students utilise AI tools in their studies and how they exercise agency in doing so. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative case study of an international student at an Australian university. The student kept a two-week digital diary documenting her uses of AI tools for coursework. A summary of her AI uses, selected diary entries and related assignment submissions informed a subsequent interview session. During the interview, the student reflected upon her interactions with the AI tools and commented on her experiences and thought processes. Her diary entries and reflections suggest that she developed notable proficiency in the use of AI applications, which she employed to complete several assessment tasks. The reflections particularly illustrate the exercise of agency in her activities of using AI, such as choosing tools to meet her study needs, adjusting written prompts to optimise outcomes and engaging in critical evaluation of AI outputs. This agentic approach challenges the deficit narrative often associated with international students, and it further complements contemporary efforts to integrate AI into higher education to enhance students’ employability and professional preparedness.

items.title: INTRODUCTION OF AN INFORMATION AND ANALYTICAL SYSTEM FOR MONITORING ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY IN UKRAINE
items.abstract: The article explores the theoretical, methodological, and applied aspects of implementing an information and analytical system for monitoring environmental safety in Ukraine, considering modern environmental challenges, the digital transformation of public administration, and European integration processes. The relevance of the topic is attributable to the growth of anthropogenic load on the environment, the consequences of military operations, the need for an operational response to environmental threats and the need to form a single information space for making management decisions in the field of environmental protection. The paper analyses the essence of environmental safety as a multidimensional category, which is considered within the framework of various scientific approaches: as the state of environmental and population protection, as a component of national security, as an object of public administration, as a risk-oriented system and as an element of the concept of sustainable development. It is substantiated that a systemic-risk-oriented approach is the most appropriate, as it allows for the complexity of environmental threats and the need to predict them to be taken into account. This paper analyses the current state of Ukraine's environmental safety monitoring system, which is characterised by a multi-level but fragmented structure, the distribution of functions between various state bodies, an insufficient level of digitalisation, and the absence of a single integrated information platform. The main problems with how the system functions have been identified. These include duplication of monitoring entity functions, an outdated material and technical base, limited automation of data collection and processing, insufficient interdepartmental coordination and a weak level of environmental risk forecasting. Particular attention is given to analysing international and European experience, especially the operation of the Eionet and Copernicus systems, and national environmental monitoring platforms in EU countries, the USA and Canada. The leading trend identified is the integration of data from various sources, the use of geoinformation technologies, satellite monitoring, big data and artificial intelligence, and ensuring open access to environmental information. A conceptual model of an information and analytical system for monitoring environmental safety has been developed. This model provides a multi-level structure, covering everything from primary data collection to analytical processing, forecasting, and management decision support. The proposed model focuses on integration with European standards, particularly INSPIRE and Copernicus, while taking into account the needs of state authorities at different levels. A SWOT analysis has been conducted to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the national monitoring system, as well as the opportunities and threats to its development. Proposals have been formulated to improve regulatory support. In particular, there is a need to adopt a special law on a unified information and analytical system for environmental safety, to unify data standards, and to implement the principles of openness of environmental information. The study proves that implementing a unified information and analytical system for monitoring environmental safety would increase the efficiency of public administration, enable environmental risks to be identified promptly, improve the quality of management decisions, make environmental policy more transparent and ensure Ukraine's sustainable development in accordance with European standards.

items.title: Introduction to GPT-5 (OpenAI)
items.abstract: This chapter provides an executive summary of GPT-5 as OpenAI’s 2025 flagship multimodal LLM, highlighting its focus on multi-step reasoning, large-context synthesis, software-engineering workflows (via GPT-5-Codex-Spark), adjustable thinking time, reliable tool use, and improved safety behaviors. It then compares GPT-5 with other leading models (GPT-4o/o3/o4, Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.x, Llama 3.x, DeepSeek) and briefly introduces the newly released GPT-5.4 and OpenAI Symphony multi-agent orchestration framework. This chapter emphasizes GPT-5’s quality-of-life improvements and positions it as a strong general-purpose model with specialized variants for coding and agentic tasks. This chapter then demonstrates GPT-5’s ability to generate Python/Matplotlib code for business-oriented and artistic visualizations. It includes examples of bar charts with alternating black/gray colors, bar charts with smooth black/gray gradient fills, labeled bar charts, and randomly generated circles. Each code listing is accompanied by a step-by-step explanation and a placeholder for the resulting figure. The examples show how GPT-5 can produce visually appealing, labeled, and gradient-filled charts with minimal prompting. The final section of this chapter explores GPT-5’s capacity to create more advanced artistic graphics using polar equations in Python/Matplotlib. It explains that no prior knowledge of polar equations is required, as the model generates complete, runnable code for visually interesting patterns. This chapter concludes by noting that some concepts (schemas, cosine similarity) are not explained in detail here and directs readers to external resources for deeper understanding. Overall, this chapter showcases GPT-5’s strength in producing both practical business graphics and esthetically pleasing mathematical art with clear code commentary. Please keep in mind that some of the code samples in this chapter involve concepts that are not explained in this chapter, such as schemas and cosine similarity. However, you can avail yourself of many free online articles that describe their purpose.

items.title: Is Influencer Identity a Key Cue? The Sequential Process of Message Acceptance in Issue-Based Communication on Social Media
items.abstract: Despite the growing use of virtual influencers (VIs), their persuasive effectiveness relative to human influencers (HIs) in issue-based social media communication remains underexplored. Drawing on social identity theory and Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) framework, Study 1 used a 2 x 2 x 2 between-subjects experiment and found higher message acceptance (MA) in the VI condition. Perceived social closeness (PSC) positively mediated the effect of influencer identity on MA, whereas trust functioned as a negative mediator. The serial pathway through PSC and trust was positive. Study 2 found no significant direct effect of influencer identity on MA, but identified perceived humanness as an upstream mediator shaping PSC, trust, and MA. Trust also worked as a negative mediator within competing mechanisms. The findings suggest that influencer identity shapes MA through layered perceptual and relational processes rather than through identity categorization alone and provide practical insights for issue-based communication.

items.title: J-tau: A Fully Localized Japanese Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction
items.abstract: We present J-tau, the first publicly available Japanese benchmark for evaluating tool-using LLM agents in interactive customer-support scenarios. While tau-bench is widely used to evaluate LLM agents, it is English-centric and cannot evaluate agents in other languages. Existing multilingual extensions offer no public Japanese version and rely primarily on machine translation, leaving locale-specific entities such as addresses and currencies inconsistent with the target region. To enable reliable evaluation in Japanese, we carefully localize tau-bench through machine translation, entity adaptation, and human review. During this process, we also uncover and fix two flaws in the original tau-bench: invalid tasks and a score aggregation error that inflates certain models' results. Experiments show that J-tau yields fewer evaluation errors than a naively machine-translated counterpart and that our fixes resolve both flaws.

items.title: JetStream: Generating Verified Query Accelerators for Existing Database Systems
items.abstract: Recent work has shown that LLMs can synthesize highly specialized database systems for fixed workloads, but these systems replace the DBMS's native storage and assume static data: users must migrate their data, often give up ad-hoc queries, and lose acceleration once the data changes. We present JetStream, which instead generates query-specific accelerators that extend an existing DBMS. Given a set of parametrized query templates, a staged agentic workflow synthesizes accelerators that run directly over the DBMS's native tables and may maintain custom auxiliary state, while the DBMS remains responsible for storage, transactions, recovery, and all other queries. A fixed, engine-neutral substrate handles engine-specific hooks and keeps auxiliary state transactionally consistent under writes. JetStream generates two kinds of accelerators: tested accelerators, which may use any optimization and are validated by differential testing, and verified accelerators which trade some performance for a machine-checked proof that every answer satisfies a trusted specification derived from the SQL. On TPC-H at SF=20, JetStream achieves a $315 \times$ geomean read speedup over DuckDB ($93 \times$ verified) and retains $120 \times$ under a continuous update stream of 10,000 modified rows per second.

items.title: KhelSaarthi: An AI-Based Sports Talent Identification System Using Flutter and Firebase
items.abstract: The KhelSaarthi mobile app is a sports assessment and training system that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies to enhance the performance of athletes by providing them with smart feedback about their movements. The proposed model combines technologies such as artificial intelligence, camera-based motion tracking and Firebase cloud services to assess the performance of the users in different sports activities. The app allows conducting automated fitness test assessments, recording the performance of the users and providing them with tips for improving their skills. The app uses the machine learning technology for analyzing the movements and providing performance scores. The app provides secure authentication and data storing with the help of Firebase integration. The proposed system is developed using Flutter technology to provide cross-platform functionality.

items.title: Kinetic modelling of Chlorella spp. wastewater treatment and resource recovery in the food industry
items.abstract: Abstract Effluents generated in the food and beverage industry typically contain elevated concentrations of organic carbon sources and inorganic nutrients, representing a significant environmental burden as global food demand continues to rise. Owing to their capacity to effectively assimilate carbon and nutrients while simultaneously generating biomass with potential valorization pathways, Chlorella spp. offers a dual benefit of contaminant removal and resource recovery. However, existing algal studies remain predominantly at the laboratory scale, and their competitive advantages have not been demonstrated for full-scale implementation. Kinetic modelling represents an essential tool to elucidate algal growth behavior, optimize operational conditions, and predict performance of algal systems for accurate scale-up, but limited studies are available to comprehensively review kinetic models of Chlorella spp. In this review, kinetic models were synthesized, including sigmoidal growth models (Gompertz, logistic, and Verhulst), single-factor and inhibition models (Monod and Andrews), light-dependent photobioreactor models (Huisman), multifactor and interaction models for co-cultures (Lotka–Volterra). Kinetic parameters from these models were compiled to support consistent projections from lab-scale to industrial-scale systems, enabling future techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment of algal systems. Other emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches, were also reviewed. The review also identified benchmark processes and outlined a decision tree for developing strategies to enhance resource recovery and phycoremediation performance. Finally, key research needs have been highlighted to guide future work in the field.

items.title: KoAGE: Do Large Language Models Know, Learn, and Coin Korean Neologisms?
items.abstract: Korean neologisms arise through diverse mechanisms, a demanding test of language models beyond lexical memorization. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce NeoTrace, an automated, rerunnable framework that collects and dates neologisms across genres. Its 4,271 entries support KoAGE, a cutoff-aware benchmark with three acquisition and two generation tasks---the latter, to our knowledge, the first to compare model coinages with attested neologisms under their original materials and community context. Across 21 models, lexical recall diverges from contextual inference: in a five-model temporal analysis, models define only 13-30% of cutoff-year words, yet can infer meaning from one usage. However, structural understanding remains limited: even correct definitions barely improve formation analysis of pre-cutoff neologisms. Given word-building materials, single models often follow human formation mechanisms, whereas multi-agent coinage favors abbreviation and depends on interaction framing. items.title: L'intégration didactique des outils de l'intelligence artificielle générative dans l'enseignement secondaire et supérieur au Maroc : Enjeux, pratiques et modélisation systémique
items.abstract: Résumé :Le présent article se propose d’examiner l'intégration didactique des technologies d'intelligence artificielle générative (IAG) au sein des établissements d'enseignement secondaire et supérieur au Maroc. Face à la mutation rapide des écosystèmes pédagogiques mondiaux et nationaux, force est de constater que l'émergence des agents conversationnels et des modèles linguistiques transforme profondément les processus d'enseignement-apprentissage, l'ingénierie des manuels scolaires et les modalités d'évaluation. S'appuyant sur un cadre théorique multidisciplinaire combinant la théorie socioconstructiviste, la théorie de la charge cognitive (Sweller) et les modèle TPACK (Mishra & Koehler), cet article formule un modèle didactique conceptuel d'ingénierie intégrée. À partir d'une méthodologie mixte combinant des observations empiriques, une analyse textuelle didactique et des enquêtes quantitatives auprès de 320 enseignants et étudiants de la région de l'Oriental, nous évaluons le niveau d'appropriation de l'IAG, la perception des compétences d'escorte pédagogique ainsi que les risques de fracture numérique et d'altération de la réflexivité. Les résultats révèlent une adhésion forte mais non structurée (74 % d'usage informel), marquée par une faible littératie IA critique et un manque d'alignement institutionnel. Nous proposons enfin des recommandations stratégiques axées sur l'éthique, la formation continue et l'innovation numérique pérenne. Mots-clés : Intelligence Artificielle Générative, Didactique, Innovation Pédagogique, Manuels Scolaires, Université Mohammed Premier, ingénierie de formation. Abstract:This prospective and analytical study examines the didactic integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools in secondary and higher education institutions in Morocco. In light of the rapid transformation of global and national educational ecosystems, the emergence of conversational agents and large language models is fundamentally altering teaching-learning processes, textbook engineering, and assessment frameworks. Grounded in a multidisciplinary theoretical framework combining socio-constructivist theory, Cognitive Load Theory (Sweller), and the TPACK model (Mishra & Koehler), this paper formulates a conceptual didactic model of integrated engineering. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach that includes empirical observations, didactic textual analysis, and quantitative surveys among 320 educators and students in the Oriental region, we evaluate the level of GAI adoption, pedagogical scaffolding competencies, and the risks of digital divide and critical reflexivity decline. Findings indicate high yet unstructured adoption (74% informal usage), characterized by limited critical AI literacy and institutional misalignment. Strategic recommendations emphasizing ethical governance, continuous professional development, and sustainable digital innovation are provided. items.title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression
items.abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. An analyst then uses verifier feedback and diagnostic tools to propose revisions, which a generator converts into refined expressions. On LLM-SRBench, L2G-SR achieves state-of-the-art numerical fit, equation level accuracy and TED across the evaluated LLM backbones and domains. L2G-SR demonstrates the value of learned structural guidance for LLM-based symbolic regression.

items.title: La Ley Silla en México: análisis de sus implicaciones legales, empresariales y de salud ocupacional
items.abstract: The "Chair Law" (Ley Silla) is a reform to Mexico's Federal Labor Law that guarantees workers the right to rest periods when their duties require them to remain standing for extended periods during the workday. Its legal foundation is established in Article 123 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States, the Federal Labor Law, and the Official Mexican Standards governing ergonomics, occupational safety, and health. The corresponding provisions came fully into force on December 15, 2025. Scientific evidence strongly supports this measure, demonstrating that prolonged standing increases the risk of venous insufficiency, lower back and neck pain, muscle fatigue, and chronic musculoskeletal disorders. Consequently, alternating between standing and sitting is widely recommended as a key preventive ergonomic strategy. Although some business sectors have expressed concerns regarding implementation costs and workplace adaptations, the long-term benefits of improved occupational health, including reduced absenteeism, lower staff turnover, and decreased medical expenses, are expected to outweigh the initial investment. Overall, this reform represents a significant step toward protecting workers' health, promoting decent working conditions, and strengthening labor rights. Nevertheless, its effectiveness will ultimately depend on adequate enforcement, monitoring, and compliance.

items.title: LabCompiler: A Framework for Verifiable Human-Machine Laboratory Execution from Imperfect Protocols
items.abstract: Closing the loop of AI-driven science requires reliably translating natural-language protocols into executable laboratory workflows despite protocol defects and heterogeneous hardware. Existing approaches often couple scientific interpretation with device-specific code generation, making errors difficult to localize and limiting reuse across laboratory platforms. We introduce LabCompiler, a robust protocol-to-execution framework that transforms imperfect natural-language protocols into verifiable human-machine workflows. Its protocol firewall diagnoses and repairs defects before compilation while preserving unaffected content, guided by troubleshooting knowledge accumulated through perturbation-guided self-evolution. A two-level, device-agnostic graph representation separates experimental semantics from hardware-specific implementation and supports capability-based device assignment with coordinated human execution. We further introduce a protocol recovery benchmark covering four controlled perturbation types and naturally occurring errors collected from protocols written by iGEM participants. Experiments show that LabCompiler outperforms frontier LLMs in protocol error correction while enabling coordinated human-machine execution across heterogeneous, partially automated laboratory settings.

items.title: Large Language Model–Assisted Qualitative Analysis: A Case Study of Medical Students with Academic Difficulties
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet practical accounts of how they can be incorporated without displacing human interpretation remain limited. This study presents a researcher-supervised workflow for processing and analysing semi-structured interviews with medical students experiencing academic difficulties. Thirty interviews were transcribed, checked against recordings, de-identified, and analysed through three stages: event/theme identification, element-level examination of focal events, and cross-event interpretive construction. The workflow identified recurring difficulties involving unclear learning goals, limited learning resources, professional-identity tension, and family expectations. LLMs supported the organisation of long transcripts and the comparison of related experiences; researchers verified outputs, retained contextual qualifications, and developed the final interpretation. The findings illustrate that LLMs can make qualitative analysis more traceable and efficient when their outputs are treated as provisional analytic material rather than authoritative conclusions. We propose practical safeguards for transcription, privacy, validation, and documentation. This case study offers a concise, reproducible pathway for using LLMs to assist—not replace—qualitative inquiry.

items.title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR SERVICE-ORIENTED COMPUTING: A CASE STUDY IN TELECOM CUSTOMER SUPPORT SYSTEMS
items.abstract: Increasingly complex telecommunications systems demand the application of intelligent and efficient methods to ensure smooth operations, sound decision-making and high-level services. With the increasing paradigm of Service-Oriented Computing (SOC) - where systems are composed of distributed services, the management of such services is becoming an even greater challenge in the customer support domain. One of the key obstacles in customer support is obtaining real time diagnostics of the problem and creating a detailed report that confirms the occurrence of the failure. This paper explores the functions and potential provided by large language models in the context of telecom customer support. The paper particularly explores the opportunities provided for automatic summarization of interactions, artificial intelligence in knowledge management and enhancement of the service diagnostics functionalities. The research is carried out through a case study, analyzing existing solutions applied in practical scenarios such as diagnostic platforms, CRM systems and AI assistants. The study explored human-in-the-loop approaches of agent feedback, which trains the AI to improve its output for better accuracy, adaptability and overall reliability. The findings revealed that Large Language Models (LLMs) boosted agent productivity, reduced human work and ensured consistency in communication. However, the output of the LLMs also presented some issues including inaccuracies and data privacy. Based on the study’s results, Large Language Models (LLMs) are actually used as a complement to human agents, enabling building more intelligent, adaptable and efficient service-oriented telecom systems.

items.title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN SEPSIS WITH HALLUCINATIONS: NARRATIVE REVIEW AND ANALYSIS OF TEN CASES
items.abstract: Objectives. Large language models (LLMs) are advancing rapidly in emergency and critical care, but the generation of “hallucinations” - unverifiable statements that contradict guidelines or extrapolate without support — remains a major patient-safety risk. Building on our previous work in Arta Medica (2024) and Healthcare Informatics Research (2026), this study characterises the prevalence, typology and potential impact of hallucinations produced by a medical LLM (Palmyra-Med 70B) in early sepsis management, based on an index case and a cohort of ten clinical vignettes. Material and Methods. Ten sepsis vignettes (eight from the open MIMIC-IV-demo database and two from the literature) were submitted to a software application based on the Palmyra-Med 70B LLM, embedded in a retrieval-augmented multi-agent system. The generated recommendations (management, antibiotics, guideline compliance with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign) were assessed independently by two ICU physicians using a standardised form; hallucinations were operationally defined and flagged by consensus. Results. The LLM produced recommendations of medium-to-high relevance and grounding (mostly 7–10/10 across both raters). Hallucinations were identified in 3 of 10 cases (Cases 1, 9 and 10), all involving the fabrication or unjustified extrapolation of clinical signs/values absent from the vignette (altered mental status, hyperlactatemia, hyperglycemia, septic shock). Non-hallucinating cases (2–8) still showed minor divergences from the guidelines, expressed as suboptimal compliance scores. Conclusions. Palmyra-Med 70B can provide useful support in the early phase of sepsis management, but requires active clinical oversight and a hybrid clinician-LLM workflow to limit hallucinations and safeguard patient safety.

items.title: Latent profiles of academic stress and exercise motivation among college students: A latent profile analysis
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the latent profile structure of academic stress and exercise motivation among Chinese college students and to examine the predictive effects of demographic variables, including gender, body mass index (BMI), grade, and household registration background, on profile membership. From May 14 to June 3, 2025, convenience cluster sampling was employed to recruit 1,346 first- to third-year undergraduate students. The participants completed the Academic Sub-Scale and the Chinese-translated Behavioral Regulation in Exercise Questionnaire-2. Latent profile analysis was performed using Mplus 8.3 to identify distinct combined patterns of academic stress and exercise motivation, and the R3STEP method was applied to test the predictive utility of demographic variables on profile assignment. Four latent profiles were identified as the best-fitting solution. Profile 1, the High stress-low motivation profile (9.0%), was characterized by elevated academic stress and low scores across all exercise motivation dimensions. Profile 2, the High stress-high motivation profile (7.4%), exhibited the highest academic stress and the highest levels of external, introjected, and identified regulation. Profile 3, the Low stress-high autonomy profile (22.1%), demonstrated the lowest academic stress and the highest intrinsic motivation. Profile 4, the Moderate-balanced adaptation profile (61.6%), was marked by moderate scores on all variables and represented the most prevalent pattern. Students with normal weight showed a significantly stronger probability association with the High stress–high motivation profile, the Low stress–high autonomy profile, and the Moderate-balanced adaptation profile compared to their overweight and obese counterparts. Female students and third-year students demonstrated a lower probability of belonging to the High stress–low motivation profile. Rural students exhibited a stronger probability association with the Low stress–high autonomy profile, whereas urban students showed a stronger probability association with the Moderate-balanced adaptation profile. Four heterogeneous combined patterns of academic stress and exercise motivation exist among Chinese college students. Normal weight, female gender, higher grade level, and rural background were positively associated with autonomous exercise motivation and may have a potential protective role in the present sample. These findings provide empirical support for the application of self-determination theory and the strength model of self-control in the context of academic stress and offer targeted references for the implementation of differentiated mental health and physical exercise interventions in higher education settings. However, due to the sampling limitations of this study, caution is warranted when extrapolating the present conclusions to the entire population of Chinese college students.

items.title: Learning by Examples: Power Grid Steady State Analysis with a Tabular Foundation Model
items.abstract: Foundation models have shown strong generalization across scientific domains, but their use in power systems remains largely task-specific. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TFM), TabPFN, can serve as a general-purpose neural solver for power grid steady-state analysis. We evaluate the TFM on three tasks: power flow (PF) prediction, N-k contingency screening (NCS), and voltage stability margin (VSM) prediction. We performed experiments on 118- and 2000-bus systems, comparing the TFM against task-specific neural baselines. Without retraining or fine-tuning, the TFM matches or outperforms the best task-specific model in several settings across the three tasks. For 118-bus PF prediction, a variant of the TFM achieves errors of $1\times 10^{-3}$ pu for voltage magnitudes and $0.30^\circ$ for voltage angles, outperforming all baselines. On unseen N-1 contingency and close-to-infeasible PF cases, the TFM is competitive with the DCPF approximation. For millions of unseen N-2 contingencies, the TFM achieves AUCs of 0.92 and 0.95 for branch and voltage violation screening, respectively. The TFM also attains accurate VSM prediction performance for the 2000-bus system with limited labelled data. The TFM attains strong results across the tested tasks despite pretraining without any power-system-specific dataset and requiring no fine-tuning step. These results offer a glimpse into the potential of pretrained TFMs as a neural solver for a range of power grid analysis tasks.

items.title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
items.abstract: In Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning, large language models may correctly infer the agent's mental state but fail to use that inference when predicting or judging the agent's subsequent actions. In this work, we investigate whether explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action with rules improves ToM reasoning. We generate concise \textit{if--then} rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks. GRPO with rule generation outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and think reasoning. Moreover, rules generated by larger models ($\geq$3B) provide transferable knowledge that improves downstream performance of GPT-4o-mini. These findings suggest that explicit rules help models bridge the reasoning gap in ToM and support knowledge transfer across models.

items.title: Learning Visual Speech Representations via Cross-Modal Distillation and Joint Face-Lip Modeling
items.abstract: Lipreading remains challenging due to the inherent ambiguity of visual speech cues and their sensitivity to head pose and video resolution. In this work, we propose FLARE, a framework for robust visual speech representation learning via cross-modal distillation and joint face-lip modeling. FLARE leverages semantically rich Whisper representations as the acoustic teacher signal, converting them into discrete distillation targets through a random-projection quantizer and pretraining the model with a masked prediction objective. To capture complementary visual information, FLARE employs a dual-stream architecture that jointly processes lip region-of-interest (ROI) and full-face inputs, where the lip stream captures finegrained articulatory motion and the face stream encodes broader facial dynamics. During pretraining, auxiliary audio input is incorporated to facilitate cross-modal alignment, and modality dropout is applied to encourage robust visual-only representations. For downstream lipreading, FLARE serves as a visual encoder coupled with either a lightweight Transformer decoder or an LLM-based decoder. Evaluated on LRS2, LRS3, and the out-of-domain WildVSR benchmark, FLARE achieves strong lipreading performance, with word error rates of 11.7%, 13.2%, and 34.3%, respectively. A progressive design study confirms the contribution of each major component. Further analyses demonstrate that joint face-lip modeling improves robustness under degraded video resolution and large head pose variation, while yielding more phoneme-discriminative visual representations. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/jxzhanggg/FLARE.

items.title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
items.abstract: User feedback enables LLMs to refine reusable personalized skills, but often mixes persistent preferences with request-specific corrections. Indiscriminately retaining both risks negative transfer, motivating selective retention at the level of individual requirements. We frame this challenge as selective transfer over atomic rules and propose SkillGrain, a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback. SkillGrain decomposes feedback into independently actionable rules, predicts their transferability, and retains only those suitable for future requests. To learn these decisions, we combine rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment that separately evaluates rule content and retention decisions. We further jointly optimize skill induction and skill-conditioned generation through reinforcement learning, ensuring that learned skills support downstream personalization. We construct a benchmark spanning five personalized writing tasks to evaluate cross-request generalization. Experiments across three base models in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings show that SkillGrain achieves the best overall average performance among competing methods.

items.title: Learning When to Trust Medical Knowledge: Regression-Safe Routing for Clinical Reasoning
items.abstract: Clinical reasoning LLMs need external medical knowledge, but retrieved evidence and reasoning chains can be outdated, poisoned, or hallucinated. Harmful knowledge can cause regression: changing a correct answer into an incorrect one. We construct a medical knowledge-poisoning benchmark covering retrieved evidence and reasoning chains, with seven attack families filtered by a three-judge "subtle-but-wrong" vote and paired clean exams that separate poisoning effects from question difficulty. No fixed knowledge-use strategy is robust across these settings: strong RAG methods trade robustness to poisoned evidence against accuracy when evidence is useful. We formulate knowledge use as per-instance routing and introduce Med-TrustRouter, a lightweight controller that keeps the solver frozen. From leakage-free runtime signals, it estimates each action's expected correctness gain and uncertainty, preserving the base answer unless another action is confidently better. Across seven medical reasoning settings, Med-TrustRouter achieves 78.9 macro and 69.2 worst-case accuracy, matching the strongest competitor on macro accuracy while substantially improving the worst-case floor. Its gains transfer across solvers and evidence judges, unlike a hand-coded router using the same signals. Similar performance across linear, tree, and neural action-value heads suggests that the benefit comes from routing rather than estimator complexity. These results support learning when to trust external knowledge for robust clinical reasoning.

items.title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
items.abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural trade-offs, deployment limitations, and future research directions for scalable and trustworthy collaborative SAR systems.

items.title: LEGAL CONFLICTS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: THE UKRAINIAN AND EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
items.abstract: This article examines the ethical and legal issues arising in the digital economy. These conflicts are conceptualised as contradictions between innovative technological practices, ethical norms and applicable legislation. Three key types of conflict are identified: those relating to privacy and data monetisation, algorithmic autonomy and accountability, and digital security and fundamental rights. Particular emphasis is placed on the wartime context in Ukraine, which presents unique challenges for digital transformation and legal regulation. Methodology. The research methodology employed is a synthesis of the comparative legal method and a Law and Economics approach. The comparative legal method is employed to compare the regulatory instruments of the European Union (GDPR, AI Act, DSA, DMA) with those of Ukraine (the Laws of Ukraine ‘On Personal Data Protection’, ‘On Virtual Assets’, ‘On Media’, and ‘On Electronic Communications’). The empirical basis of the study comprises reports by the European Commission (Digital Economy and Society Index, DESI), Eurostat statistical data on the digital transformation of EU Member States, and analytical materials published by the OECD (Digital Economy Outlook) and the World Bank (Digital Development Report). The Law and Economics analysis is employed to evaluate the impact of legal conflicts on the investment climate, transaction costs and innovation activity. Results. The study demonstrates that the development of the digital economy in Ukraine and the European Union is determined not only by the pace of digital technology adoption, but also by the quality of the institutional environment in which digital markets operate. The European model is distinguished by the establishment of common rules governing data flows, the utilisation of artificial intelligence, and the operation of digital platforms. This contributes to a reduction in regulatory uncertainty for businesses and the creation of conditions conducive to long-term investment in digital technologies. Ukraine continues to face an institutional and technological gap with the EU, as evidenced by uneven levels of business digitalisation, limited investment capacity among some businesses in digital infrastructure, and heightened risks associated with the use of data and artificial intelligence technologies. At the same time, a lack of clear rules governing the digital economy could lead to higher transaction costs for businesses, reduce investment activity and make it more difficult for Ukrainian companies to access the European digital market. The study establishes that digital regulatory conflicts have not only legal but also direct economic effects: they affect regulatory compliance costs, the level of market competition, access to digital services, consumer trust, and the ability of businesses to scale digital business models. In this context, the harmonisation of Ukraine's digital environment with European approaches may be regarded as one of the factors reducing institutional barriers to digital investment and deepening Ukraine's economic integration with the EU. Practical Implications. The practical value of the findings lies in their potential application to shaping Ukraine's economic policy on digital transformation, aimed not merely at regulatory adaptation but, above all, at creating conditions to increase enterprise productivity, attract investment, and expand the participation of Ukrainian firms in European digital markets. Priority areas include reducing regulatory and transaction costs for digital businesses; establishing rules for data flows and AI deployment that align with the European market; promoting the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises; developing digital infrastructure; and encouraging competition in digital markets. The implementation of these measures takes on additional economic significance under martial law, as digital technologies can ensure business continuity, reduce the costs of coordinating economic processes and boost enterprise resilience to external shocks. Therefore, the effectiveness of harmonisation with European digital regulations should be assessed not only by the number of provisions implemented, but also by their impact on investment activity, productivity, competitiveness and the resilience of Ukraine’s digital economy. Value / Originality. The scientific novelty of the study lies in its identification of the economic consequences of regulatory and ethico-legal conflicts arising during the digital transformation of Ukraine's economy and its integration into the European digital space. The proposed typology of key conflicts enables the systematisation of factors that generate regulatory uncertainty, increase transaction costs, and affect investment activity and the competitiveness of digital economy enterprises. The developed cyclical model of conflict evolution is intended as a tool for identifying the interrelationship between technological change, regulatory adaptation, economic costs, and institutional responses. Its application may prove useful in assessing the digital resilience of the economy, underpinning public policy on digital transformation, and setting priorities for Ukraine's economic integration into the European digital market amid wartime conditions and post-conflict recovery.

items.title: Let Me Clarify: Interactive Modeling of Soft Attributes
items.abstract: People commonly express preferences through soft attributes such as is interesting,'' which are difficult to operationalize for computational preference modeling. Latent representations can obscure how such attributes are interpreted, limiting transparency and user control. We formalize softness as the diversity of valid interpretations a description permits and provide empirical support for this characterization. Our proposed measure estimates softness to guide clarification and determine when to generate computational approximations. This is instantiated in AttriFy, a mixed-initiative system that translates descriptions into executable Python functions over text corpora. An interactive dashboard connects the dialogue to proposed functions and computed values, enabling users to inspect, accept, reject, and refine interpretations. An exploratory within-subjects study with 32 participants compares our softness-guided clarification approach with an LLM baseline in supporting interpretable attribute construction. This work positions softness as a basis for constructing explicit, user-steerable attribute dimensions for downstream preference elicitation and decision-making.

items.abstract: This chapter examines the role of educational technologies in facilitating effective online academic advising through a qualitative case study approach in a higher education institution. The study explores the use of Learning Management Systems, virtual communication platforms, student information systems, analytics dashboards, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported tools, and online scheduling systems within academic advising practices. Using thematic analysis, the findings identify key dimensions influencing advising effectiveness, including technology-enabled flexibility, improved advisor–student communication, personalized advising support, AI-supported efficiency, digital literacy challenges, and the continuing importance of human interaction in advising relationships.

items.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities
items.abstract: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.

items.title: Lightweight 3D Convolutional Networks for Biomechanical Motion Analysis in Martial Arts Training
items.abstract: To reduce the subjectivity of traditional martial arts training assessment and avoid the deployment requirements of wearable devices, the study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted analysis system based on a 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN). This study adopts a 3D CNN as the backbone network and develops optimization strategies from four aspects. Spatiotemporal decomposition convolution factorizes standard 3D convolution kernels into a combination of spatial convolution and temporal convolution. The temporal attention mechanism adaptively computes the importance weight of each frame, enabling the model to focus on key action frames. A dynamic inference mechanism determines whether computation should be terminated early based on the confidence of intermediate-layer outputs, thereby reducing redundant computation. Knowledge distillation uses only the class-similarity soft distribution of a large teacher model to supervise the lightweight student model. This reduces the loss of feature representation caused by network compression and helps maintain recognition accuracy with fewer parameters. Experimental results are obtained on the Chain-of-Thought Action Form Assessment (CoT-AFA) and Martial Arts, Dancing and Sports Dataset (MADS) public datasets. The results show that the proposed method achieves a Top-1 accuracy of 74.2% on the CoT-AFA dataset, which is close to the 75.3% achieved by Video Swin Transformer. Meanwhile, the proposed method reduces the number of parameters by approximately 52.3% (14.2M vs. 29.8M) and decreases Floating Point Operations per Second by approximately 43.7% (52.4G vs. 93.0G). In addition, the mean squared error (MSE) for quality evaluation is reduced to 1.48. On the MADS dataset, the Top-1 accuracy reaches 68.9%, while the mean per-joint position error is reduced to 60.5 mm. The results support the use of the system for video-based analysis in martial arts training.

items.title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?
items.abstract: AI-text detection generally asks whether a machine wrote a text. As AI becomes an increasingly integral and accepted part of writing, the more relevant question is no longer whether AI was used, but how much of the text reflects human contribution. A prominent line of work estimates this by measuring how predictive a person's prompt is of the final text. We show that this measure can be easily manipulated. We introduce SPECIFICITY PADDING that simply asks the model to copy a few random IDs from the prompt, and that alone makes a title-only request look more human than one that supplies the article's key ideas. A context-swap audit then holds each document fixed, and only shows or hides the IDs to the evaluator. The score of the unchanged text swings by a third to half of its scale, and it rises for every document we test, on news and scientific abstracts, across varied LLMs from 3.8B to 753B parameters. The same articles can average 85\% human or 15\% human depending only on which prompt is on record, and even with no prompt at all, the output-only variant rewards the random strings themselves. An exact identity, the credit ledger, explains why. The score is a surprisal-weighted average over the text, so rare strings that the context makes copyable collect the credit, whatever they mean. A two-point bound marks a deeper limit. If the prompt could have been machine-written, every transcript-only method must, in the worst case, miss by half the contribution at stake. Likelihood-based scores alone cannot reliably establish human contribution without evidence of what the person added and how the text was produced.
